rows.text: The front face is a mana engine; the back face is the deck. The Prismatic Bridge puts a creature or planeswalker from your library onto the battlefield at the beginning of every upkeep — free, uncastable, uncounterable — and this deck is built out of six- and seven-mana planeswalkers precisely because it never intends to pay for them. Everything else either protects the Bridge, doubles the loyalty, or untaps the walkers.

rows.name: Esika, God of the Tree
rows.text: cast the front face for {G}{G} when you need mana and fixing: she taps for any colour and gives your other legendary creatures the same ability.

Cast The Prismatic Bridge when you need the engine. A free planeswalker every upkeep wins the game on its own if it survives two turns, and nothing in a normal Commander game answers an enchantment quickly.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep fixing and acceleration. Five colours and a six-mana commander is the deck's real cost — Sol Ring, the Moxen and the land-fetch spells are what make turn four or five possible.

Choose the face deliberately. Esika for two mana is a ramp piece when you are behind on mana; The Prismatic Bridge for six is the engine when you are not. Casting the wrong one is the most common mistake.
Doubling Season before a planeswalker, always. The same Elspeth is a value engine without it and an immediate emblem with it.

rows.name: Norn's Annex
rows.text: prioritise it once you have two walkers out. Your walkers are the win condition and combat is the only thing that reliably kills them.
